name: John Muir
tagline: Scottish farm boy who became the father of America's national parks

immigration.arrived: Fountain Lake farm near Portage, Wisconsin
immigration.detail: In 1849 Daniel Muir, a strict Presbyterian shopkeeper, took eleven-year-old John and two siblings to America to farm. The boy cleared land from dawn to dark, read by candlelight, and taught himself mathematics and mechanics.

summary: An immigrant farm boy, factory inventor and thousand-mile walker, John Muir fell in love with the Sierra Nevada in 1868 and spent the rest of his life persuading Americans, including President Theodore Roosevelt, that wild places must be protected. Yosemite National Park and the Sierra Club are his monuments.

biography.text: John Muir was born in Dunbar, Scotland, on April 21, 1838. In 1849 his father moved the family to a farm in central Wisconsin, where John laboured through his teens while reading every book he could borrow. A gifted mechanic, he carved clocks, barometers and an 'early-rising machine' that tipped its sleeper out of bed, and in 1860 exhibited his inventions at the Wisconsin State Fair before studying for two years at the University of Wisconsin.

In 1867, while working in an Indianapolis carriage-parts factory, a file slipped and pierced his right eye; he lay blind in a darkened room for weeks. When his sight returned he resolved to see the world instead of machines, walked a thousand miles from Indiana to the Gulf of Mexico, and in 1868 sailed to California. Asked the way out of San Francisco, he said he wanted to go 'anywhere that is wild', and headed for Yosemite.

Muir spent years in the Sierra Nevada as a shepherd, sawmill hand and self-taught scientist. He argued, against the leading geologists of the day, that Yosemite Valley had been carved by glaciers, and found living glaciers to prove it. His magazine articles and books, including The Mountains of California (1894) and My First Summer in the Sierra (1911), brought the high country to readers across the nation.

In 1889 he camped with Century magazine editor Robert Underwood Johnson and launched the campaign that created Yosemite National Park on October 1, 1890, a week after Sequoia. In 1892 he co-founded the Sierra Club and served as its first president for the rest of his life. In May 1903 he took President Theodore Roosevelt camping for three nights in Yosemite, a trip that helped persuade Roosevelt to place Yosemite Valley under federal protection and to expand national forests and monuments.

Muir lost his final battle, to stop San Francisco from damming the Hetch Hetchy Valley inside Yosemite, in 1913, and died in Los Angeles on December 24, 1914. His home in Martinez, California, is now the John Muir National Historic Site, his papers are preserved at the University of the Pacific, and Muir Woods National Monument carries his name.

achievements.title: Campaign that created Yosemite National Park
achievements.description: His Century magazine articles with Robert Underwood Johnson led Congress to establish Yosemite National Park on October 1, 1890.

achievements.title: Co-founder and first president of the Sierra Club
achievements.description: Led the club from its founding on May 28, 1892 until his death, making it the model for citizen conservation groups.

achievements.title: Glacial theory of Yosemite
achievements.description: Correctly argued that glaciers, not a cataclysm, had shaped Yosemite Valley.

achievements.title: Camping trip with Theodore Roosevelt
achievements.description: Three nights in Yosemite that influenced Roosevelt's conservation policy.

achievements.title: Author of twelve books and some 300 articles
achievements.description: Including The Mountains of California, Our National Parks, My First Summer in the Sierra and The Yosemite.

honors.title: Muir Woods National Monument named in his honour

John Muir Trail, Yosemite to Mount Whitney, completed

quotes.text: The mountains are calling and I must go.
quotes.context: Letter to his sister Sarah Muir Galloway, September 3, 1873

quotes.text: Everybody needs beauty as well as bread, places to play in and pray in, where nature may heal and give strength to body and soul alike.

fun_facts.text: Muir's 'early-rising machine', a bed that tipped its occupant onto the floor at a set hour, is displayed at the Wisconsin Historical Society.
He once rode out a Sierra windstorm by climbing to the top of a hundred-foot Douglas fir to feel how trees experience the wind.

discussion_prompts: Muir went from building machines to protecting wilderness. Can an accident or setback change the direction of a life for the better?
He convinced a president by taking him camping. What is the most persuasive thing someone has ever shown you, rather than told you?
Muir lost the fight over Hetch Hetchy. Why do we remember some defeats as victories?

review_notes.ihh_statement: Helped establish Sequoia (1890), Yosemite (1898), Mount Rainier (1899), and Grand Canyon (1908) National Parks.
review_notes.finding: Yosemite National Park was established on October 1, 1890, not 1898. Grand Canyon became a national monument in 1908 and a national park in 1919.
Muir's naturalization has been questioned by historians; some have found no record that he formally became a citizen. Recommend verifying with the National Archives before publishing a date.

review_notes.ihh_statement: His three-day camping trip with President Theodore Roosevelt persuaded the president to create the National Parks System.
review_notes.finding: The National Park Service was created in 1916, two years after Muir's death. The 1903 trip influenced Roosevelt's conservation policy, including the 1906 transfer of Yosemite Valley to federal control.
